newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - French oil firms fume as shops sell petrol.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - French oil firms fume as shops sell petrol.

text.p: France's oil industry, already under siege from striking truckers, added discrimination to its list of grievances on Thursday as more petrol stations were commandeered by local authorities to ease fuel shortages.

The association which represents top oil companies, UFIP, said rival supermarkets had been spared the decision in many places to requisition stations for emergency use and ration petrol to ordinary motorists.
"The prefects (local government officials are only requisitioning traditional stations and not the supermarkets, and that's harming us a lot," an UFIP spokeswoman said.
Supermarkets sell around half the petrol in France.
Oil companies were also angry at the lack of security for forecourt attendants who had to cope with frustrated and sometimes aggressive motorists.
"There are a lot of problems on the ground -- scuffles, security problems -- especially near Marseilles and Bordeaux," the UFIP spokeswoman said.
Service stations were impounded and rationing introduced in 34 French departments, or counties, on Wednesday.
Government officials said the figure was expected to reach 40 areas -- nearly half the French total -- on Thursday.
Police were called earlier to several petrol stations where irate motorists refused to allow emergency vehicles, including doctors' cars, to jump queues.
Petrol was running scarce as truckers completed their blockade of all 13 French oil refineries and ringed off around half of the country's fuel storage depots, preventing delivery.
Nearly all the fuel bought by ordinary drivers is delivered from refineries by road tanker. The rest goes by pipeline.
UFIP said at least 2,500 of France's 18,000 service stations were either short of fuel or out of it altogether on Thursday.
However a key depot near the capital had been freed from the blockade, delaying the point at which Parisians might start to feel the pinch. So far the impact is mainly in the south.
A spokesman for Elf Aquitaine, France's largest oil firm, said 55 percent of its 1,500 main service stations were missing some or all of their regular fuel supply.
Elf was also forced to shut two refineries for a day in a separate strike over job cuts at distribution unit Elf Antar.
A spokesman said the large Donges refinery in western France and the Feyzin refinery serving Lyon in the southeast stopped producing for about 24 hours from Thursday morning.
Elf Antar workers had already shut down Elf's smaller Grandpuits refinery near Paris for a day from Wednesday.
Oil companies warned all French refineries would probably have to slow down production by the weekend, or next week at the latest, if the 11-day-old truckers' blockade continued to bite.
Acute petrol shortages in the southeast even threatened to maroon people working inside oil refineries.
One senior manager at a refinery near Marseilles told Reuters he had problems finding petrol to get to work, but it would be illegal to tap his own giant complex even for a few litres.
"All refineries are out of bounds as far as Customs are concerned. It would be a tax fraud. We don't even have a pump."
